Tolerance was defined as no immunological or histological signs of CD while consuming gluten. Sixty-six patients accepted participation, but after review of the diagnostic biopsies 53 were found to have true CD. Twenty-three percent of patients had a gluten-containing diet, 15% admitted gluten transgression and 62% followed the GFD. Patients on a GFD had significantly more osteoporosis. Normal small bowel mucosa was found in four of eight on gluten-containing diet and in four of four with gluten transgression. Two patients were considered to have developed tolerance to gluten. One of them was HLA-DQ2/DQ8 negative.
input: Question: Gluten tolerance in adult patients with celiac disease 20 years after diagnosis?
output: Development of tolerance to gluten seems possible in some patients with CD. Further follow-up will show whether this tolerance is permanent or only a long-term return to latency. This feature may be associated with genetic characteristics, especially with HLA genotypes that differ from DQ2 or DQ8. More insight into the mechanisms of the development of gluten tolerance may help to distinguish those CD patients that might not require life-long GFD.
llm_output: In summary, while some adult patients with celiac disease may develop tolerance to gluten, it is not common and requires careful evaluation. The majority of patients, even those who have been on a gluten-free diet for 20 years, are likely to remain intolerant to gluten. However, the possibility of developing tolerance should be considered in individual cases, and regular monitoring is essential.

instruction: Answer the question based on the following context: The US Preventive Services Task Force recommends against spirometry in the absence of symptoms. However, as much as 50% of COPD cases in the United States remain undiagnosed. Report of symptoms, smoking history, and spirometric data were collected from subjects screened for a work-related medical evaluation (N = 3,955). Prevalence of airflow obstruction and respiratory symptoms were assessed. Sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values, and relative risks of predicting symptoms and smoking history for COPD were calculated. Forty-four percent of smokers in our sample had airways obstruction (AO). Of these, 36% reported a diagnosis of or treatment for COPD. Odds ratio (95% CI) for AO with smoking (>or = 20 pack-years) was 3.73 (3.12- 4.45), 1.98 (1.73-2.27) for cough, 1.79 (1.55-2.08) for dyspnea, 1.95 (1.70-2.34) for sputum, and 2.59 (2.26-2.97) for wheeze. Respiratory symptoms were reported by 92% of smokers with AO, 86% smokers with restriction, 76% smokers with normal spirometry, and 73% of nonsmokers. Sensitivity (92% vs 90%), specificity (19% vs 22%), positive (47% vs 40%) and negative (75% vs 80%) predictive values for the presence of one or more symptoms were similar between smokers and all subjects.
input: Question: Do symptoms predict COPD in smokers?
output: COPD is underdiagnosed in the United States. Symptoms are frequent in subjects with AO and increase their risk for COPD, but add little beyond age and smoking history to the predictive value of spirometry. In view of the high prevalence of symptoms and their poor predictive value, a simpler and more effective approach would be to screen older smokers.
llm_output: Symptoms can be used to predict COPD in smokers, but their predictive value is limited. The study found that 44% of smokers in the sample had airway obstruction (AO), with 36% reporting a diagnosis of or treatment for COPD. The odds ratios for AO were significant for smoking history, cough, dyspnea, sputum, and wheeze, indicating that these symptoms are associated with an increased likelihood of AO. However, the sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values for the presence of one or more symptoms were similar between smokers and all subjects, suggesting that while symptoms may be indicative, they are not highly specific or sensitive on their own. Therefore, while symptoms can provide some indication of COPD in smokers, they should be considered alongside other clinical data such as smoking history and spirometric results for a more accurate diagnosis.

instruction: Answer the question based on the following context: Web search engines are an important tool in communication and diffusion of knowledge. Among these, Google appears to be the most popular one: in August 2008, it accounted for 87% of all web searches in the UK, compared with Yahoo's 3.3%. Google's value as a diagnostic guide in general medicine was recently reported. The aim of this comparative cross-sectional study was to evaluate whether searching Google with disease-related terms was effective in the identification and diagnosis of complex immunological and allergic cases. Forty-five case reports were randomly selected by an independent observer from peer-reviewed medical journals. Clinical data were presented separately to three investigators, blinded to the final diagnoses. Investigator A was a Consultant with an expert knowledge in Internal Medicine and Allergy (IM&A) and basic computing skills. Investigator B was a Registrar in IM&A. Investigator C was a Research Nurse. Both Investigators B and C were familiar with computers and search engines. For every clinical case presented, each investigator independently carried out an Internet search using Google to provide a final diagnosis. Their results were then compared with the published diagnoses. Correct diagnoses were provided in 30/45 (66%) cases, 39/45 (86%) cases, and in 29/45 (64%) cases by investigator A, B, and C, respectively. All of the three investigators achieved the correct diagnosis in 19 cases (42%), and all of them failed in two cases.
input: Question: Search engine as a diagnostic tool in difficult immunological and allergologic cases: is Google useful?
output: This Google-based search was useful to identify an appropriate diagnosis in complex immunological and allergic cases. Computing skills may help to get better results.
llm_output: Based on the study, Google can be considered a useful tool in the diagnosis of difficult immunological and allergologic cases. The results showed that using Google for these cases was effective, with the correct diagnosis being provided in 66% (Investigator A), 86% (Investigator B), and 64% (Investigator C) of the cases. Additionally, all three investigators achieved the correct diagnosis in 42% of the cases, indicating a significant level of agreement and effectiveness. However, it is important to note that while Google can be a valuable resource, it should not be the sole diagnostic tool, and its use should be complemented with other clinical and diagnostic methods.

instruction: Answer the question based on the following context: Various factors contribute to the effective implementation of evidence-based treatments (EBTs). In this study, cognitive processing therapy (CPT) was administered in a Veterans Affairs (VA) posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) specialty clinic in which training and supervision were provided following VA implementation guidelines. The aim was to (a) estimate the proportion of variability in outcome attributable to therapists and (b) identify characteristics of those therapists who produced better outcomes. We used an archival database of veterans (n = 192) who completed 12 sessions of CPT by therapists (n = 25) who were trained by 2 nationally recognized trainers, 1 of whom also provided weekly group supervision. Multilevel modeling was used to estimate therapist effects, with therapists treated as a random factor. The supervisor was asked to retrospectively rate each therapist in terms of perceived effectiveness based on supervision interactions. Using single case study design, the supervisor was interviewed to determine what criteria she used to rate the therapists and emerging themes were coded. When initial level of severity on the PTSD Checklist (PCL; McDonald&Calhoun, 2010; Weathers, Litz, Herman, Huska,&Keane, 1993) was taken into account, approximately 12% of the variability in the PCL at the end of treatment was due to therapists. The trainer, blind to the results, identified the following characteristics and actions of effective therapists: effectively addressing patient avoidance, language used in supervision, flexible interpersonal style, and ability to develop a strong therapeutic alliance.
input: Question: Uniformity of evidence-based treatments in practice?
output: This study adds to the growing body of literature documenting the importance of the individual therapist as an important factor in the change process.
llm_output: The study on the implementation of cognitive processing therapy (CPT) in a Veterans Affairs (VA) posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) specialty clinic provides insights into the uniformity of evidence-based treatments in practice. The aim was to estimate the proportion of variability in treatment outcomes attributable to therapists and identify characteristics of those therapists who produced better outcomes. Using multilevel modeling, it was found that approximately 12% of the variability in the PTSD Checklist (PCL) scores at the end of treatment was due to differences among therapists, after accounting for the initial level of severity. This suggests that while there is some variability in outcomes based on the therapist, the majority of the outcome variability is likely due to other factors such as patient characteristics and the effectiveness of the CPT itself. The trainer, who was blind to the results, identified several characteristics and actions of effective therapists, including effectively addressing patient avoidance, using appropriate language in supervision, having a flexible interpersonal style, and the ability to develop a strong therapeutic alliance. These findings indicate that while there is a degree of variability in the effectiveness of CPT as delivered by different therapists, the overall treatment is relatively uniform and effective when implemented according to VA guidelines. Therefore, the study supports the idea that evidence-based treatments like CPT can be consistently and effectively implemented in practice, with the identified characteristics of effective therapists contributing to the quality and consistency of the treatment.

instruction: Answer the question based on the following context: The seafaring industry remains a hazardous occupation that requires sophisticated systems of risk and fitness assessment. This study aims to investigate the extent of agreement between Approved Doctors (ADs) and Medical Referees (MRs) when they assess a seafarer's fitness. Between 2003 and 2009 a total of 232,878 seafarer medical examinations were carried out by ADs, of which 465 were considered by the MRs because the seafarer appealed against the AD's decision. The extent of agreement between ADs and MRs was studied. Two hundred and sixty-eight (58%) cases seen by the ADs were classed as category 4 "permanently unfit"; the referees only placed 85 (18%) of them in this category. On the other hand, 252 (54%) cases seen by the MRs were classed as category 2 "fit with restrictions", while the ADs had only placed 111 (24%) in this category. The overall agreement between the assessors (AD vs. MR) was poor (Kappa K = 0.18). For cardiovascular diseases and for mental ill-health, access to additional information by the MR was the commonest reason for changing the fitness category, but for all other conditions factors such as the experience and knowledge of the MRs or their different interpretation of the standards were the most frequent reasons for a change to fitness category or to restrictions.
input: Question: Do approved doctors and medical referees in the UK agree when assessing a seafarer's fitness?
output: This study found that there was poor agreement between the AD's decision and the subsequent MR's decision regarding the fitness of those seafarers who decided to appeal against the AD's initial assessment. The reasons for this are considered.
llm_output: Based on the study conducted between 2003 and 2009, the agreement between Approved Doctors (ADs) and Medical Referees (MRs) in the UK when assessing a seafarer's fitness is found to be poor. The overall Kappa statistic (K) for the agreement was 0.18, which indicates a low level of agreement beyond what would be expected by chance. This conclusion is supported by the significant differences in the classification of seafarers' fitness categories: 58% of cases classified as category 4 "permanently unfit" by ADs were only 18% by MRs, and 54% of cases classified as category 2 "fit with restrictions" by MRs were only 24% by ADs. The primary reasons for these discrepancies include the access to additional information by MRs, particularly in cases of cardiovascular diseases and mental ill-health, as well as differences in the experience, knowledge, and interpretation of the standards by the assessors.

instruction: Answer the question based on the following context: Hepatorenal syndrome (HRS) is the functional renal failure associated with advanced cirrhosis and has also been described in fulminant hepatic failure. Without liver transplantation its prognosis is dismal. Our study included patients with type 1 HRS associated with cirrhosis, who were not liver transplant candidates.AIM: To identify variables associated with improved survival. Sixty-eight patients fulfilled the revised Ascites Club Criteria for type 1 HRS. None of them was suitable for liver transplantation. All the patients were treated with combinations of: albumin, midodrine and octreotide, pressors, and hemodialysis. Median survival was 13 days for the whole group. Survival varied with the end-stage liver disease (ESLD) etiology: autoimmune, 49 days, cardiac cirrhosis, 22 days, idiopathic, 15.5 days, viral, 15 days, hepatitis C and alcohol, 14.5 days, alcohol 8 days, and neoplasia 4 days (p = 0.048). Survival of HRS associated with alcoholic liver disease versus other etiologies was not statistically significant (p = 0.1). Increased serum creatinine (p = 0.02) and urinary sodium 6-10 mEq/l (p = 0.027) at the initiation of therapy were prognostic factors for mortality. HRS treatment modalities (p = 0.73), use of dialysis (p = 0.56), dialysis modality (p = 0.35), use of vasopressors (p = 0.26), pre-existing renal disease (p = 0.49), gender (p = 0.90), and age (p = 0.57) were not associated with survival.
input: Question: Hepatorenal syndrome: are we missing some prognostic factors?
output: We report for the first time ESLD etiology as a prognostic factor for survival. The renal function (expressed as serum creatinine) and urinary Na (<5 mEq/l) at the time of diagnosis were found to be associated with survival, suggesting that early treatment might increase survival.
llm_output: Hepatorenal syndrome (HRS) is a condition characterized by functional renal failure in patients with advanced cirrhosis or fulminant hepatic failure. The prognosis for HRS, especially in the absence of liver transplantation, is generally poor. In the context of the study, several factors were considered to identify variables associated with improved survival in patients with type 1 HRS associated with cirrhosis who are not liver transplant candidates. The following points highlight the findings and suggest potential areas where additional prognostic factors might be considered: \\n1. **End-Stage Liver Disease (ESLD) Etiology**: The survival rates varied based on the underlying cause of ESLD. For example, patients with autoimmune etiology had a longer median survival (49 days) compared to those with other etiologies such as cardiac cirrhosis, idiopathic, viral, and alcohol-related liver disease. This suggests that the etiology of the liver disease is a significant prognostic factor. \\n2. **Serum Creatinine and Urinary Sodium**: Increased serum creatinine levels (p = 0.02) and urinary sodium 6-10 mEq/l (p = 0.027) at the initiation of therapy were identified as prognostic factors for mortality. These markers indicate the severity of renal dysfunction and electrolyte imbalance, which are critical in the management of HRS. \\n3. **Treatment Modalities**: While the study evaluated the impact of various treatment modalities, including albumin, midodrine, octreotide, pressors, and hemodialysis, the results showed that these treatments did not significantly affect survival. However, the effectiveness of these treatments in managing symptoms and improving quality of life should still be considered. \\n4. **Other Potential Prognostic Factors**: The study did not find significant associations between survival and factors such as the use of dialysis, dialysis modality, vasopressors, pre-existing renal disease, gender, or age. However, further research could explore additional factors such as the presence of hepatopulmonary syndrome, the severity of ascites, and the patient's overall nutritional status, which may also influence outcomes. \\nIn summary, while the study identified some key prognostic factors, there may be other factors that are not yet fully understood or considered. Further research is needed to comprehensively understand the multifaceted nature of HRS and to identify all potential prognostic factors.

instruction: Answer the question based on the following context: Although dose-volume parameters in image-guided brachytherapy have become a standard, the use of posterior-inferior border of the pubic symphysis (PIBS) points has been recently proposed in the reporting of vaginal doses. The aim was to evaluate their pertinence. Nineteen patients who received image-guided brachytherapy after concurrent radiochemotherapy were included. Per treatment, CT scans were performed at Days 2 and 3, with reporting of the initial dwell positions and times. Doses delivered to the PIBS points were evaluated on each plan, considering that they were representative of one-third of the treatment. The movements of the applicator according to the PIBS point were analysed. Mean prescribed doses at PIBS -2, PIBS, PIBS +2 were, respectively, 2.23 ± 1.4, 6.39 ± 6.6, and 31.85 ± 36.06 Gy. Significant differences were observed between the 5 patients with vaginal involvement and the remaining 14 at the level of PIBS +2 and PIBS: +47.60 Gy and +7.46 Gy, respectively (p = 0.023 and 0.03). The variations between delivered and prescribed doses at PIBS points were not significant. However, at International commission on radiation units and measurements rectovaginal point, the delivered dose was decreased by 1.43 ± 2.49 Gy from the planned dose (p = 0.019). The delivered doses at the four points were strongly correlated with the prescribed doses with R(2) ranging from 0.93 to 0.95. The movements of the applicator in regard of the PIBS point assessed with the Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine coordinates were insignificant.
input: Question: Vaginal dose assessment in image-guided brachytherapy for cervical cancer: Can we really rely on dose-point evaluation?
output: The doses evaluated at PIBS points are not impacted by intrafractional movements. PIBS and PIBS +2 dose points allow distinguishing the plans of patients with vaginal infiltration. Further studies are needed to correlate these parameters with vaginal morbidity.
llm_output: In the context of vaginal dose assessment in image-guided brachytherapy for cervical cancer, the use of dose-point evaluation, particularly at the posterior-inferior border of the pubic symphysis (PIBS) points, has been explored. The study included 19 patients who received image-guided brachytherapy after concurrent radiochemotherapy. CT scans were performed at Days 2 and 3, with reporting of the initial dwell positions and times. Doses delivered to the PIBS points were evaluated, considering that they represent one-third of the treatment. The movements of the applicator according to the PIBS point were analyzed. The mean prescribed doses at PIBS -2, PIBS, PIBS +2 were 2.23 ± 1.4, 6.39 ± 6.6, and 31.85 ± 36.06 Gy, respectively. Significant differences were observed between the 5 patients with vaginal involvement and the remaining 14 at the level of PIBS +2 and PIBS: +47.60 Gy and +7.46 Gy, respectively (p = 0.023 and 0.03). The variations between delivered and prescribed doses at PIBS points were not significant. However, at the International Commission on Radiation Units and Measurements (ICRU) rectovaginal point, the delivered dose was decreased by 1.43 ± 2.49 Gy from the planned dose (p = 0.019). The delivered doses at the four points were strongly correlated with the prescribed doses, with R² ranging from 0.93 to 0.95. The movements of the applicator in regard to the PIBS point, assessed with Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine (DICOM) coordinates, were insignificant. Based on these findings, while the PIBS points provide a reasonable approximation of the vaginal dose, the significant difference in the rectovaginal point and the strong correlation between delivered and prescribed doses suggest that dose-point evaluation can be a reliable method for vaginal dose assessment in image-guided brachytherapy for cervical cancer. However, it is important to consider the specific clinical context and potential variations in patient anatomy and treatment delivery.

instruction: Answer the question based on the following context: Stock et al. (Eur Respir J 25:47-53, 2005) recently estimated asthma prevalence in Germany using claims data on prescriptions and hospital diagnoses and found high prevalence peaks in infants. Our objective was to critically assess and discuss various aspects of identifying children with asthma using prescription data. We replicated the selection procedure of Stock et al. using data on 290,919 children aged 0-17 years insured in the Gmünder ErsatzKasse (GEK) in 2005. Asthma prevalence was also estimated in a sample of 17,641 children aged 0-17 years participating in the German Health Interview and Examination Survey for Children and Adolescents (KiGGS) from 2003 to 2006. In children aged 0-4 years insured in the GEK, prevalences were found to range from 11.7 to 17.7% for boys and from 7.2 to 11.1% for girls when the criteria of Stock et al. were applied. A steady decline in prevalences was observed in older age groups. Asthma prevalence estimated in the KiGGS data showed a quite different distribution. In the age group 0-4 years, prevalences were found to range from 0 to 2.6% in boys and from 0 to 1.0% in girls; in children>4 years, prevalences were found to increase with increasing age.
input: Question: Prescriptions as a proxy for asthma in children: a good choice?
output: When additional validation studies were taken into account, asthma medications were found to be prescribed not only for asthma but also for other respiratory diseases. In addition, not all children with current asthma had prescriptions. We therefore conclude that asthma medications are therefore not a good proxy for the disease.
llm_output: The use of prescriptions as a proxy for asthma in children has both advantages and limitations. On one hand, prescription data can provide a clear indication of asthma management, showing which children are being treated with asthma medications. This can be particularly useful in identifying children who are actively managing their asthma symptoms. On the other hand, there are several potential issues with using prescriptions alone to identify children with asthma. Firstly, not all children with asthma may be prescribed medication, especially if their symptoms are mild or if they do not have a diagnosed condition. Secondly, some children may be prescribed asthma medications for other conditions, leading to potential overestimation of asthma prevalence. Additionally, the type and frequency of prescriptions can vary based on factors such as the severity of asthma, the presence of comorbidities, and the specific healthcare provider's approach. Therefore, while prescriptions can be a useful tool in identifying children with asthma, they should be used in conjunction with other diagnostic and clinical information to ensure accurate identification and management of asthma in children.

instruction: Answer the question based on the following context: Parental drinking has been shown to be associated with offspring drinking. However, the relationship appears to be more complex than often assumed and few studies have tracked it over longer time periods. To explore the long-term (10-year) transmission of familial drinking during adolescence to offspring drinking patterns in young adulthood. Swedish longitudinal study, assessing the relationship between familial drinking in 2000 and offspring drinking in 2010 using simultaneous quantile regression analysis (n=744).DATA: Data on familial drinking was gathered from the Swedish level-of-living surveys (LNU) and from partner LNU in 2000 while data on offspring drinking in young adulthood was gathered from LNU 2010. Drinking among offspring, parents and potential stepparents was measured through identical quantity-frequency indices referring to the past 12 months in 2010 and 2000 respectively. Young adults whose families were abstainers in 2000 drank substantially less across quintiles in 2010 than offspring of non-abstaining families. The difference, however, was not statistically significant between quintiles of the conditional distribution. Actual drinking levels in drinking families were not at all or weakly associated with drinking in offspring. Supplementary analyses confirmed these patterns.
input: Question: Does the familial transmission of drinking patterns persist into young adulthood?
output: The association between familial drinking and offspring drinking in young adulthood exhibits clear non-linear trends. Changes in the lower part of the familial drinking distribution are strongly related to drinking in young adults, but the actual levels of drinking in drinking families appear less important in shaping the drinking patterns of the offspring in young adulthood.
llm_output: The familial transmission of drinking patterns does have a persistent effect into young adulthood, but the relationship is more nuanced than a simple direct transmission. The study indicates that young adults whose families were abstainers in 2000 tended to drink substantially less across quintiles in 2010 compared to those from non-abstaining families. However, it's important to note that the difference in drinking levels between these groups was not statistically significant when examining the conditional distribution of the data. Additionally, the actual drinking levels within drinking families were not strongly associated with the drinking behaviors of their offspring. These findings suggest that while there is a general trend for familial drinking patterns to influence offspring drinking, the association is not consistently strong or significant across all measures and subgroups.

instruction: Answer the question based on the following context: To investigate the effect of fenofibrate on sleep apnoea indices. Proof-of-concept study comprising a placebo run-in period (1 week, 5 weeks if fibrate washout was required) and a 4-week randomized, double-blind treatment period. Thirty-four subjects (mean age 55 years, body mass index 34 kg/m 2 , fasting triglycerides 3.5 mmol/L) with diagnosed sleep apnoea syndrome not treated with continuous positive airways pressure were enrolled and randomized to once daily treatment with fenofibrate (145 mg NanoCrystal(R) tablet) or placebo. Overnight polysomnography, computerized attention/vigilance tests and blood sampling for measurement of lipids, insulin, fasting plasma glucose and fibrinogen were performed at the end of each study period. NCT00816829. As this was an exploratory study, a range of sleep variables were evaluated. The apnoea/hypopnoea index (AHI) and percentage of time spent with arterial oxygen saturation (SpO(2))<90% were relevant as they have been evaluated in other clinical trials. Other variables included total apnoeas, hypopnoeas and oxygen desaturations, and non-cortical micro-awakenings related to respiratory events per hour. Fenofibrate treatment significantly reduced the percentage of time with SpO(2)<90% (from 9.0% to 3.5% vs. 10.0% to 11.5% with placebo, p = 0.007), although there was no significant change in the AHI (reduction vs. control 14% (95%CI -47 to 40%, p = 0.533). Treatment reduced obstructive apnoeas (by 44%, from 18.5 at baseline to 15.0 at end of treatment vs. 29.0 to 30.5 on placebo, p = 0.048), and non-cortical micro-awakenings per hour (from 23.5 to 18.0 vs. 24.0 to 25.0 with placebo, p = 0.004). Other sleep variables were not significantly influenced by fenofibrate. Exploratory study in patients with mild to moderate sleep apnoea, limited treatment duration; concomitant hypnotic treatment (35%); lack of correction for multiplicity of testing.
input: Question: Proof of concept study: does fenofibrate have a role in sleep apnoea syndrome?
output: The consistent direction of change in sleep indices in this proof-of-concept study may support further investigation of fenofibrate in moderate to severe sleep apnoea syndrome.
llm_output: Fenofibrate, a fibrate medication, has shown potential in the management of sleep apnoea syndrome based on an exploratory proof-of-concept study. The study, which involved 34 subjects with diagnosed sleep apnoea not treated with continuous positive airways pressure (CPAP), aimed to evaluate the effect of fenofibrate on various sleep-related parameters. Key findings from the study include a significant reduction in the percentage of time spent with arterial oxygen saturation (SpO2) <90% during fenofibrate treatment compared to placebo, indicating an improvement in nocturnal hypoxemia. Additionally, fenofibrate was associated with a reduction in obstructive apnoeas and non-cortical micro-awakenings per hour, suggesting a positive impact on sleep quality and structure. However, it is important to note that the apnoea/hypopnoea index (AHI) did not show a significant change, and the study's limitations, such as its exploratory nature and the use of concomitant hypnotic treatments in 35% of participants, should be considered when interpreting these results. Further research, including larger and more comprehensive clinical trials, is needed to confirm the role of fenofibrate in the treatment of sleep apnoea syndrome.

instruction: Answer the question based on the following context: To determine the potential prognostic value of using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to identify patients with disorders of consciousness, who show potential for recovery. Observational study. Unit for acute rehabilitation care. Patients (N=22) in a vegetative state (VS; n=10) and minimally conscious state (MCS; n=12) during the first 200 days after the initial incident. Not applicable. Further course on the Coma Recovery Scale-Revised. Participants performed a mental imagery fMRI paradigm. They were asked to alternately imagine playing tennis and navigating through their home. In 14 of the 22 examined patients (VS, n=5; MCS, n=9), a significant activation of the regions of interest (ROIs) of the mental imagery paradigm could be found. All 5 patients with activation of a significant blood oxygen level dependent signal, who were in a VS at the time of the fMRI examination, reached at least an MCS at the end of the observation period. In contrast, 5 participants in a VS who failed to show activation in ROIs, did not (sensitivity 100%, specificity 100%). Six of 9 patients in an MCS with activation in ROIs emerged from an MCS. Of 3 patients in an MCS who did not show activation, 2 patients stayed in an MCS and 1 patient emerged from the MCS (sensitivity 85%, specificity 40%).
input: Question: Can mental imagery functional magnetic resonance imaging predict recovery in patients with disorders of consciousness?
output: The fMRI paradigm mental imagery displays a high concordance with the further clinical course of patients in a VS. All 5 patients in a VS who showed significant activation of ROIs had a favorable further course until the end of the observation period. We therefore propose the term "functional minimally conscious state" for these patients. They may benefit from rehabilitation treatment. In cases where no significant activation was seen, the method has no prognostic value. Prediction of the clinical course of patients in an MCS by fMRI was considerably less accurate than in patients in a VS.
llm_output: Mental imagery functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) can predict recovery in patients with disorders of consciousness. The study found that 14 out of 22 examined patients, including 5 in a vegetative state (VS) and 9 in a minimally conscious state (MCS), showed significant activation of the regions of interest (ROIs) during the mental imagery fMRI paradigm. All 5 patients with significant blood oxygen level dependent (BOLD) signal activation who were in a VS at the time of the fMRI examination reached at least an MCS by the end of the observation period. Additionally, 6 out of 9 patients in an MCS with ROI activation emerged from the MCS. While these results are promising, it is important to note that the sensitivity and specificity of the test vary depending on the initial state of the patient, with higher accuracy observed in patients initially in a VS.

instruction: Answer the question based on the following context: To compare the accuracy achieved by a trained urology nurse practitioner (UNP) and consultant urologist in detecting bladder tumours during flexible cystoscopy. Eighty-three patients underwent flexible cystoscopy by both the UNP and consultant urologist, each unaware of the other's findings. Before comparing the findings, each declared whether there was tumour or any suspicious lesion requiring biopsy. Of 83 patients examined by flexible cystoscopy, 26 were found to have a tumour or a suspicious lesion. One tumour was missed by the UNP and one by the urologist; each tumour was minute. Analysis using the chance-corrected proportional agreement (Kappa) was 0.94, indicating very close agreement.
input: Question: The nurse cystoscopist: a feasible option?
output: A UNP can be trained to perform cystoscopy and detect suspicious lesions as accurately as can a consultant urologist. Legal and training issues in implementation are important.
llm_output: Based on the study comparing the accuracy of a trained urology nurse practitioner (UNP) and a consultant urologist in detecting bladder tumors during flexible cystoscopy, the results suggest that the UNP is a viable and accurate option. The Kappa value of 0.94 indicates very close agreement between the UNP and the urologist, with only one tumor missed by the UNP and one by the urologist. This level of accuracy, especially for a non-physician, demonstrates that the UNP can effectively perform and interpret flexible cystoscopies, making it a feasible option for bladder tumor detection.

instruction: Answer the question based on the following context: Although consensus guidelines for pretreatment evaluation and monitoring of propranolol therapy in patients with infantile hemangiomas (IH) have been formulated, little is known about the cardiovascular side effects. We sought to analyze cardiovascular evaluations in patients with IH at baseline and during treatment with an oral beta-blocker. Data from 109 patients with IH were retrospectively analyzed. Patient and family history, pretreatment electrocardiogram (ECG), heart rate, and blood pressure were evaluated before initiation of beta-blocker therapy. Blood pressure and standardized questionnaires addressing side effects were evaluated during treatment. Questionnaire analyses (n = 83) identified 3 cases with a family history of cardiovascular disease in first-degree relatives. ECG findings were normal in each case and no serious complication of therapy occurred. ECG abnormalities were found in 6.5% of patients but there were no contraindications to beta-blocker therapy and no major complications. Hypotension in 9 patients did not require therapy adjustment. In all, 88 parents (81%) reported side effects during beta-blocker treatment. The relatively small patient cohort is a limitation.
input: Question: Is cardiovascular evaluation necessary prior to and during beta-blocker therapy for infantile hemangiomas?
output: Pretreatment ECG is of limited value for patients with an unremarkable cardiovascular history and a normal heart rate and blood pressure. Hypotension may occur during treatment.
llm_output: Cardiovascular evaluation is indeed necessary prior to and during beta-blocker therapy for infantile hemangiomas. This conclusion is supported by the findings of the study, which highlights the importance of thorough cardiovascular assessments in this context. Specifically, the study conducted pretreatment electrocardiogram (ECG) and other cardiovascular evaluations, including patient and family history, heart rate, and blood pressure, before initiating beta-blocker therapy. During treatment, they monitored blood pressure and used standardized questionnaires to address side effects. The results showed that while ECG abnormalities were found in 6.5% of patients, there were no contraindications to beta-blocker therapy and no major complications. Additionally, hypotension in 9 patients did not require therapy adjustment. The study also noted that 88 parents (81%) reported side effects during beta-blocker treatment. These findings underscore the need for careful cardiovascular monitoring to ensure the safety and efficacy of beta-blocker therapy in patients with infantile hemangiomas.

instruction: Answer the question based on the following context: Implementation of the complex treatment strategies that have been shown to improve survival of patients with congestive heart failure (CHF) may require certain expertise. We wanted to examine the association between pattern of outpatient care and survival of patients with CHF. In a retrospective cohort study conducted with national Veterans Health Administration (VHA) databases, we examined the association between the pattern of outpatient care and survival in 11,661 patients discharged from VA hospitals between October 1, 1991, and September 30, 1992, with the primary diagnosis of CHF (cohort 1). Patients were divided into 4 groups, on the basis of their pattern of outpatient care over a 12-month period after discharge: 1) general medicine clinic visits only (GM-only); 2) cardiology clinic visits only (CARD-only); 3) general medicine and cardiology (MIXED) clinic visits; and 4) neither general medicine nor cardiology clinic visits (no-GM/CARD). We used the Cox proportional hazards model to evaluate 1-year survival, controlling for clinical and demographic factors. Consistency of our results was examined by performing identical analysis on a cohort of patients discharged from VHA hospitals between October 1, 1994, and September 30, 1995 (cohort 2, n = 10,141). The overall 1-year mortality rate was 23% in the primary cohort. The unadjusted mortality rate was highest for patients in the no-GM/CARD follow up (29%) and lowest for patients in the MIXED group (19%). By use of the MIXED group as reference and adjusting for important clinical and demographic factors, the risk of death (risk ratio [95% CI]) was 1.12 (0.94-1.34) in the CARD-only group, 1.26 (1.15-1.38) in the GM-only group, and 1.48 (1.28-1.72) in the no-GM/CARD group. Cohort-2 results were consistent with cohort 1 for most covariates, and significant survival differences were again found between GM-only and the MIXED group (1.25 [1.14-1.37]).
input: Question: Is specialty care associated with improved survival of patients with congestive heart failure?
output: We found an improved survival associated with cardiologist care and a mixture of general practitioner and cardiologist care compared with general practitioner care. The pattern of outpatient care may therefore be important for the survival of patients with CHF.
llm_output: Based on the study, the pattern of outpatient care was associated with survival in patients with congestive heart failure (CHF). The overall 1-year mortality rate was 23% in the primary cohort, with the highest unadjusted mortality rate in the no-GM/CARD group (29%) and the lowest in the MIXED group (19%). After adjusting for clinical and demographic factors, the risk of death was increased in the CARD-only group (1.12 [0.94-1.34]), GM-only group (1.26 [1.15-1.38]), and no-GM/CARD group (1.48 [1.28-1.72]) compared to the MIXED group. These results suggest that a combination of general medicine and cardiology care (MIXED) is associated with improved survival in patients with CHF. Therefore, the study indicates that specialty care, particularly when combined with general medicine, is associated with improved survival in patients with congestive heart failure.

instruction: Answer the question based on the following context: To identify the features of PMR that may predict the duration of steroid therapy, the occurrence of relapses and the late development of GCA. Prospective cohort study of 176 patients with PMR, followed up for 5 years. Baseline factors associated with the duration of steroids therapy were identified using Cox regression. Predictors of relapse and the late development of GCA were identified using binary logistic regression. A total of 176 patients with PMR were included, of whom 124 stopped steroids within 5 years. The probability of stopping steroids within 5 years was independently reduced by an elevated plasma viscosity (PV) [hazard ratio (HR) = 0.49; 95% CI 0.29, 0.82 for a PV>or = 2.00 mPa s compared with a PV<or = 1.80 mPa s; overall P = 0.024] and by starting treatment at>15 mg prednisolone (HR = 0.63; 95% CI 0.41, 0.97; P = 0.036). Either of these independently reduced the chances of stopping steroids within a given time interval between 27 and 51%. No significant predictors of relapse were identified. Predictors of late GCA on univariable analysis were female sex [odds ratio (OR) = 8.16; 95% CI 1.06, 63.13; P = 0.044], HLA-DRB1*0101 or -*0401 alleles (OR = 4.95; 95% CI 1.05, 23.34; P = 0.043), PV>or = 2.00 mPa s compared with PV<or = 1.80 mPa s (OR = 10.64; 95% CI 1.28, 88.38; P = 0.029) and initial prednisolone dose>15 mg (OR = 4.53; 95% CI 1.61, 12.79; P = 0.004).
input: Question: Can the prognosis of polymyalgia rheumatica be predicted at disease onset?
output: A higher PV in PMR increases the risk of prolonged steroid therapy and late GCA. Female sex and particular HLA alleles may increase the risk of late GCA. Starting patients on>15 mg prednisolone is associated with a prolonged steroid duration.
llm_output: Polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) is a condition characterized by muscle pain and stiffness, primarily affecting the shoulders, neck, and hips. The prognosis of PMR can indeed be predicted at disease onset based on several factors. A study involving 176 patients with PMR, followed up for 5 years, identified certain baseline factors that are associated with the duration of steroid therapy, occurrence of relapses, and the late development of giant cell arteritis (GCA). Elevated plasma viscosity (PV) and starting treatment at a higher dose of prednisolone (>15 mg) were found to independently reduce the probability of stopping steroids within 5 years. Specifically, an elevated PV (≥2.00 mPa s) and a higher initial prednisolone dose (>15 mg) were significant predictors, reducing the chances of discontinuing steroids by 27-51%. Additionally, factors such as female sex, HLA-DRB1*0101 or *0401 alleles, and initial prednisolone dose >15 mg were identified as predictors of late GCA. However, it's important to note that while these factors can help in predicting the prognosis, they do not provide a definitive outcome and should be considered in the context of individual patient management.

instruction: Answer the question based on the following context: Ascitis and undernutrition are frequent complications of cirrhosis, however ascitis volume and anthropometric assessment are not routinely documented or considered in prognostic evaluation. In a homogeneous cohort followed during two years these variables were scrutinized, aiming to ascertain relevance for longterm outcome. Population (N = 25, all males with alcoholic cirrhosis) was recruited among patients hospitalized for uncomplicated ascitis. Exclusion criteria were refractory or tense ascitis, cancer, spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, bleeding varices and critical illness. Measurements included ultrasonographically estimated ascitis volume, dry body mass index/BMI , upper arm anthropometrics, hematologic counts and liver function tests. Population (age 48.3 ± 11.3 years, BMI 21.1 ± 3.5 kg/m², serum albumin 2.5 ± 0.8 g/dL) was mostly in the Child-Pugh C category (77.8%) but clinically stable. During the follow-up period of 22.6 ± 3.8 months, additional hospitalizations numbered 1.7 ± 1.0 and more than one quarter succumbed. Admission ascitis volume corresponded to 7.1 ± 3.6 L and dry BMI to 18.3 ± 3.5 kg/m². Child Pugh index was relevant for both mortality and rehospitalization. Nevertheless, similar matches for mortality were documented with ascitis volume and dry BMI, and arm circumference below the 5th percentile was highly significantly associated with rehospitalization.
input: Question: Should ascitis volume and anthropometric measurements be estimated in hospitalized alcoholic cirrotics?
output: A greater association than hitherto acknowledged, between ascitis volume and anthropometric measurements from one side, and long-term rehospitalization and mortality from the other, was demonstrated in male stable alcoholic cirrhotics. Further studies with alcoholic and other modalities of cirrhosis including women are recommended.
llm_output: Based on the study's findings, it is reasonable to consider that ascitis volume and anthropometric measurements, such as dry BMI and arm circumference, could be valuable in the prognostic evaluation of hospitalized alcoholic cirrotics. The study demonstrated that these parameters, along with the Child-Pugh index, were associated with both mortality and rehospitalization. Specifically, ascitis volume and dry BMI showed significant correlations with mortality, while arm circumference below the 5th percentile was highly significantly associated with rehospitalization. Therefore, incorporating these measurements into the clinical assessment may provide a more comprehensive understanding of the patient's condition and potential outcomes.

instruction: Answer the question based on the following context: To illustrate how maternal mortality audit identifies different causes of and contributing factors to maternal deaths in different settings in low- and high-income countries and how this can lead to local solutions in reducing maternal deaths. Descriptive study of maternal mortality from different settings and review of data on the history of reducing maternal mortality in what are now high-income countries. Kalabo district in Zambia, Farafenni division in The Gambia, Onandjokwe district in Namibia, and the Netherlands. Population of rural areas in Zambia and The Gambia, peri-urban population in Namibia and nationwide data from The Netherlands. Data from facility-based maternal mortality audits from three African hospitals and data from the latest confidential enquiry in The Netherlands. Maternal mortality ratio (MMR), causes (direct and indirect) and characteristics. MMR ranged from 10 per 100,000 (the Netherlands) to 1540 per 100,000 (The Gambia). Differences in causes of deaths were characterized by HIV/AIDS in Namibia, sepsis and HIV/AIDS in Zambia, (pre-)eclampsia in the Netherlands and obstructed labour in The Gambia.
input: Question: The use of audit to identify maternal mortality in different settings: is it just a difference between the rich and the poor?
output: Differences in maternal mortality are more than just differences between the rich and poor. Acknowledging the magnitude of maternal mortality and harnessing a strong political will to tackle the issues are important factors. However, there is no single, general solution to reduce maternal mortality, and identification of problems needs to be promoted through audit, both national and local.
llm_output: The use of maternal mortality audit to identify maternal mortality in different settings is not just a difference between the rich and the poor, but it reflects a spectrum of healthcare challenges and systemic issues that vary across low- and high-income countries. The study highlights that while the maternal mortality ratio (MMR) can range widely, from 10 per 100,000 in the Netherlands to 1540 per 100,000 in The Gambia, the underlying causes and contributing factors are multifaceted and context-specific. In the Netherlands, the MMR is low due to comprehensive healthcare systems, effective management of pregnancy complications, and strong public health infrastructure. In contrast, in The Gambia, the high MMR is attributed to a combination of factors including limited access to healthcare, high rates of HIV/AIDS, and other indirect causes. The audit process in these settings aims to uncover these specific causes and contributing factors, which can then inform targeted interventions. For instance, in Namibia, the focus might be on addressing HIV/AIDS, while in Zambia, the emphasis could be on managing sepsis and (pre-)eclampsia. The audit is a tool for identifying these issues, but the solutions require a broader, more nuanced approach that addresses the root causes and systemic challenges. Therefore, the use of maternal mortality audit is a critical step in understanding and reducing maternal mortality, but it is part of a larger, more complex effort that involves improving healthcare access, addressing underlying health conditions, and strengthening public health systems.

instruction: Answer the question based on the following context: The effect of neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) on topographical distribution patterns of lymph node metastasis in cervical cancer was unknown. Patients with FIGO stage IB1-IIB who underwent radical surgery with or without NACT were enrolled (3527 patients). A matched-case comparison design was used to compare the effects of NACT on lymph node metastasis. We analyzed groups of 167 and 140 patients who were diagnosed with lymph node metastasis in the matched primary surgery group and NACT group, respectively, and no significant difference was observed (p = 0.081). The incidence of lymph node metastasis was significantly decreased in the NACT-responsive group compared to the non-responsive group (18.4% vs. 38.6%, P<0.001). The metastatic rates for every lymph node group also declined in the NACT-responsive group except for the deep inguinal and the para-aortic lymph node groups. Clinical response, deep stromal, parametrial and lymph vascular invasions were independent risk factors for lymph node metastasis in the NACT group. Furthermore, deep stromal invasion and lymph vascular invasion, but not the response to NACT, were independently associated with upper LNM. The number of lymph nodes involved, response to NACT, tumor histology and a positive vaginal margin were independent prognostic factors affecting DFS or OS rates in node-positive patients treated with NACT plus radical surgery.
input: Question: Could the extent of lymphadenectomy be modified by neoadjuvant chemotherapy in cervical cancer?
output: The frequency and topographic distribution of LNM are not modified by NACT, and clinical non-responders showed more involved LNs. A systemic and extensive lymphadenectomy should be performed in patients treated with NACT plus surgery regardless of the response to NACT.
llm_output: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) in cervical cancer has been shown to influence the extent of lymphadenectomy, but the modification is not universal across all lymph node groups. Specifically, NACT has been found to decrease the incidence of lymph node metastasis, particularly in certain lymph node groups. The metastatic rates for most lymph node groups declined in the NACT-responsive group, except for the deep inguinal and para-aortic lymph node groups. This suggests that while NACT can reduce the need for extensive lymphadenectomy in many cases, it may not be as effective in modifying the extent of lymphadenectomy in the deep inguinal and para-aortic regions. Therefore, the extent of lymphadenectomy can be modified by NACT in cervical cancer, but the effect is more pronounced in some lymph node groups than others.

instruction: Answer the question based on the following context: Blood stream infection (BSI) and the subsequent development of sepsis are among the most common infection complications occurring in severe burn patients. This study was designed to evaluate the relationship between the burn wound flora and BSI pathogens. Documentation of all bacterial and fungal wound and blood isolates from severe burn patients hospitalized in the burn unit and intensive care unit was obtained from medical records retrieved retrospectively from a computerized, hospital-wide database over a 13-year period. All data were recorded in relation to the Ryan score. Of 195 severe burn patients, 88 had at least 1 BSI episode. Transmission of the same pathogen from wound to blood was documented in 30% of the patients, with a rising BSI frequency as the Ryan score increased. There were a total of 263 bacteremic episodes in 88 study patients, 44% of blood isolates were documented previously in wound cultures, and transmission of the same pathogen from wound to blood was noted in 65% of bacteremic patients.
input: Question: Do Wound Cultures Give Information About the Microbiology of Blood Cultures in Severe Burn Patients?
output: When there is clinical suspicion of sepsis, appropriate empirical systemic antibiotic therapy should be broad spectrum and should rely on the susceptibility of the organisms from recent cultures of the burn wound surface, until the blood cultures results are completed.
llm_output: Wound cultures do provide information about the microbiology of blood cultures in severe burn patients. The study indicates that there is a significant relationship between the burn wound flora and the pathogens causing blood stream infections (BSIs). Specifically, 44% of the blood isolates were previously documented in wound cultures, and transmission of the same pathogen from the wound to the blood was noted in 65% of bacteremic patients. This suggests that wound cultures can be a valuable source for identifying potential BSI pathogens, especially in severe burn patients where the risk of infection is high. However, it is important to note that while wound cultures can provide useful information, they may not always capture the full spectrum of pathogens present in blood cultures, and other diagnostic methods may be necessary for comprehensive evaluation.

instruction: Answer the question based on the following context: Longitudinal cohort studies in sub-Saharan Africa are urgently needed to understand cardiovascular disease development. We, therefore, explored health behaviours and conventional risk factors of African individuals with optimal blood pressure (BP) (≤ 120/80 mm Hg), and their 5-year prediction for the development of hypertension. The Prospective Urban Rural Epidemiology study in the North West Province, South Africa, started in 2005 and included African volunteers (n = 1994; aged>30 years) from a sample of 6000 randomly selected households in rural and urban areas. At baseline, 48% of the participants were hypertensive (≥ 140/90 mmHg). Those with optimal BP (n = 478) were followed at a success rate of 70% for 5 years (213 normotensive, 68 hypertensive, 57 deceased). Africans that became hypertensive smoked more than the normotensive individuals (68.2% vs 49.8%), and they also had a greater waist circumference [ratio of geometric means of 0.94 cm (95% CI: 0.86-0.99)] and greater amount of γ-glutamyltransferase [0.74 U/l (95% CI: 0.62-0.88)]at baseline. The 5-year change in BP was independently explained by baseline γ-glutamyltransferase [R(2) = 0.23, β = 0.13 U/l (95% CI: 0.01-0.19)]. Alcohol intake also predicted central systolic BP and carotid cross-sectional wall area (CSWA) at follow-up. Waist circumference was another predictor of BP changes [β = 0.18 cm (95% CI: 0.05-0.24)]and CSWA. HIV infection was inversely associated with increased BP.
input: Question: Are behavioural risk factors to be blamed for the conversion from optimal blood pressure to hypertensive status in Black South Africans?
output: During the 5 years, 24% of Africans with optimal BP developed hypertension. The surge in hypertension in Africa is largely explained by modifiable risk factors. Public health strategies should focus aggressively on lifestyle to prevent a catastrophic burden on the national health system.
llm_output: The conversion from optimal blood pressure (BP) to hypertensive status in Black South Africans is influenced by a combination of behavioral and other risk factors. Key behavioral risk factors that have been identified include smoking, alcohol intake, and waist circumference. Smoking was found to be more prevalent among those who developed hypertension compared to those who remained normotensive. Specifically, 68.2% of individuals who became hypertensive smoked, compared to 49.8% of normotensive individuals. Additionally, alcohol intake was associated with an increase in central systolic BP and carotid cross-sectional wall area (CSWA) at follow-up. Increased waist circumference, which is a marker of central obesity, was also linked to greater BP changes and CSWA. These findings suggest that these behavioral risk factors play a significant role in the development of hypertension in this population. However, it is important to note that while these factors are significant, they are not the only contributors, and other factors such as HIV infection, which was inversely associated with increased BP, also play a role.

instruction: Answer the question based on the following context: The gap between evidence-based treatments and routine care has been well established. Findings from the Sequenced Treatments Alternatives to Relieve Depression (STAR*D) emphasized the importance of measurement-based care for the treatment of depression as a key ingredient for achieving response and remission; yet measurement-based care approaches are not commonly used in clinical practice. The Nine-Item Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9) for monitoring depression severity was introduced in 19 diverse psychiatric practices. During the one-year course of the project the helpfulness and feasibility of implementation of PHQ-9 in these psychiatric practices were studied. The project was modeled after the Institute for Healthcare Improvement Breakthrough Series. Two of the 19 practices dropped out during the course of the project. By the conclusion of the study, all remaining 17 practices had adopted PHQ-9 as a routine part of depression care in their practice. On the basis of responses from 17 psychiatrists from those practices, PHQ-9 scores influenced clinical decision making for 93% of 6,096 patient contacts. With the additional information gained from the PHQ-9 score, one or more treatment changes occurred during 40% of these clinical contacts. Changing the dosage of antidepressant medication and adding another medication were the most common treatment changes recorded by psychiatrists, followed by starting or increasing psychotherapy and by switching or initiating antidepressants. In 3% of the patient contacts, using the PHQ-9 led to additional suicide risk assessment.
input: Question: Systematic use of patient-rated depression severity monitoring: is it helpful and feasible in clinical psychiatry?
output: The study findings suggest that adopting measurement-based care, such as using the PHQ-9, is achievable, even in practices with limited resources.
llm_output: The systematic use of patient-rated depression severity monitoring, specifically the PHQ-9, has been shown to be both helpful and feasible in clinical psychiatry. The study conducted in 19 diverse psychiatric practices demonstrated that the PHQ-9 can be effectively integrated into routine care. By the end of the one-year project, all remaining 17 practices had adopted the PHQ-9 as a standard part of their depression care. The PHQ-9 scores influenced clinical decision-making for 93% of the 6,096 patient contacts, indicating its utility in guiding treatment. Additionally, the use of PHQ-9 led to treatment changes in 40% of the clinical contacts, with common changes including adjusting antidepressant dosages, adding medications, and increasing psychotherapy. The tool also prompted additional suicide risk assessments in 3% of the patient contacts, highlighting its role in identifying patients at higher risk. These findings support the feasibility and effectiveness of the PHQ-9 in enhancing the management of depression in clinical settings.

instruction: Answer the question based on the following context: To explore the secondary benefits of treadmill training for people in the chronic stage of recovery from stroke. Modified random assignment, matched-pair control group design with repeated measures. Outpatient stroke centre. Twenty individuals post first stroke who acknowledged walking slower than pre stroke. Participants matched by side of hemiparesis and motor impairment. Twelve 20-minute sessions of walking on a treadmill or weekly phone call. Depression (Beck Depression Index), mobility and social participation (Stroke Impact Scale 3.0 subscales) were assessed initially, at the end of 12 treatments (four weeks) and six weeks later. No significant difference was found between groups for any dependent measure. The ANOVA to investigate main effects in each group found no significant findings in the control group; however in the treatment group significant improvements over time for depression (P = 0.005, P<0.001), mobility (P = 0.008) and social participation (P = 0.004) were demonstrated.
input: Question: Treadmill training post stroke: are there any secondary benefits?
output: A task-specific intervention designed to improve gait speed may potentially provide secondary benefits by positively impacting depression, mobility and social participation for people post stroke.
llm_output: Treadmill training post-stroke can have several secondary benefits, even though the primary goal is to improve walking ability. The context provided suggests that the study aimed to explore these secondary benefits. Here are some of the potential secondary benefits based on the information and the outcomes mentioned in the context: 1. **Depression**: Treadmill training may help in reducing symptoms of depression. The study found significant improvements in depression scores (P = 0.005, P<0.001) in the treatment group over time. This indicates that regular physical activity, such as treadmill training, can contribute to better mental health and mood regulation. 2. **Mobility**: While the primary focus is on walking, the study also observed significant improvements in mobility (P = 0.008) in the treatment group. Enhanced mobility can lead to greater independence and quality of life for individuals post-stroke. 3. **Social Participation**: Treadmill training might indirectly enhance social participation. The study noted significant improvements in social participation (P = 0.004) in the treatment group. Increased mobility and better physical function can encourage individuals to engage more actively in social activities, thereby improving their social well-being. These secondary benefits highlight the importance of treadmill training not just for physical recovery but also for overall well-being and reintegration into daily life.

instruction: Answer the question based on the following context: To study the relationship between lunar position and the day of delivery; to investigate the synodic distribution of spontaneous deliveries, especially in relation to the presence of a full moon. Retrospective analysis of 1248 spontaneous full-term deliveries in three-year period (36 lunar months), setted at Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Civil Hospital, Fano (Marche, Italy), using circular statistics techniques. A connection between the distribution of spontaneous full-term deliveries and the lunar month was found. The effect of the phases of the moon seems to be particularly relevant in multiparae and plurigravidae; in these cases, the mean day of delivery corresponds to the first or second day after the full moon.
input: Question: Does lunar position influence the time of delivery?
output: In this paper the effect of lunar phases on the time of delivery is shown. This influence seems to be especially relevant in the case of multiparae and plurigravidae. Nevertheless, it is too weak to allow for prediction regarding the days with the highest frequency of deliveries.
llm_output: Based on the study conducted at the Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Civil Hospital, Fano (Marche, Italy), there is evidence suggesting that lunar position does influence the time of delivery. The research, which involved a retrospective analysis of 1248 spontaneous full-term deliveries over a three-year period (36 lunar months), utilized circular statistics techniques to investigate the synodic distribution of these deliveries, particularly in relation to the presence of a full moon. The findings indicated a connection between the distribution of spontaneous full-term deliveries and the lunar month. Specifically, the mean day of delivery for multiparae and plurigravidae corresponds to the first or second day after the full moon, highlighting the relevance of the moon's phases in this context. Therefore, the conclusion is that lunar position, particularly the full moon, appears to have an influence on the timing of spontaneous full-term deliveries, especially in women who have given birth before (multiparae) and those who are pregnant for the second time (plurigravidae).

instruction: Answer the question based on the following context: Patients transported by helicopter often require advanced airway management. The purpose of this study was to determine whether or not the in-flight environment of air medical transport in a BO-105 helicopter impairs the ability of flight nurses to perform oral endotracheal intubation. The study was conducted in an MBB BO-105 helicopter. Flight nurses performed three manikin intubations in each of the two study environments: on an emergency department stretcher and in-flight in the BO-105 helicopter. The mean time required for in-flight intubation (25.9 +/- 10.9 seconds) was significantly longer than the corresponding time (13.2 +/- 2.8 seconds) required for intubation in the control setting (ANOVA, F = 38.7, p<.001). All intubations performed in the control setting were placed correctly in the trachea; there were two (6.7%) esophageal intubations in the in-flight setting. The difference in appropriate endotracheal intubation between the two settings was not significant (chi 2 = 0.3; p>0.05).
input: Question: Is oral endotracheal intubation efficacy impaired in the helicopter environment?
output: Oral endotracheal intubation in the in-flight setting of the BO-105 helicopter takes approximately twice as long as intubation in a ground setting. The results support pre-flight intubation of patients who appear likely to require urgent intubation during air medical transport in the BO-105 helicopter.
llm_output: The study indicates that while the in-flight environment in a BO-105 helicopter does not significantly impair the ability of flight nurses to perform oral endotracheal intubation, it does affect the time required to complete the procedure. Specifically, the mean time for in-flight intubation was 25.9 seconds, which is significantly longer than the 13.2 seconds required in the control setting (emergency department stretcher). However, the rate of successful tracheal intubation was similar between the two settings, with all intubations in the control setting being correct and only 6.7% (2 out of 30) being esophageal intubations in the in-flight setting. Therefore, the conclusion is that the efficacy of oral endotracheal intubation, in terms of success rate, is not significantly impaired in the helicopter environment, but the time required for the procedure is increased.

instruction: Answer the question based on the following context: To report an uncommon association of prostate and lung cancer. The characteristics of both tumors, their association with tumors in other sites and the time of presentation are analyzed. Both tumors were in the advanced stages. Metastatic carcinoma of the prostate was discarded due to the form of presentation.
input: Question: Prostatic syndrome and pleural effusion: are they different diseases?
output: Although the association of prostate and lung cancer is uncommon, the possibility of synchronous tumors should be considered in patients with urinary and pulmonary symptoms suggestive of neoplasm. It is important to determine if the lesion is a metastasis, since the prognosis depends on the second tumor.
llm_output: Prostatic syndrome and pleural effusion are not necessarily different diseases, but rather, they can be associated with different underlying conditions. Prostatic syndrome typically refers to a set of symptoms and findings related to the prostate gland, such as benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), prostatitis, or prostate cancer. Pleural effusion, on the other hand, is the accumulation of fluid in the pleural space, which can be caused by various conditions including heart failure, liver disease, kidney disease, or cancer. While these two conditions can occur independently, in some cases, they may be related through an underlying disease, such as metastatic cancer, where the cancer can affect both the prostate and the pleura. Therefore, it is important to consider the patient's overall clinical picture and any potential underlying conditions that might be causing both the prostatic syndrome and the pleural effusion.

instruction: Answer the question based on the following context: Each patient received a smartphone with an insulin dose advisor (IDA) and with (G3 group) or without (G2 group) the telemonitoring/teleconsultation function. Patients were classified as "high users" if the proportion of "informed" meals using the IDA exceeded 67% (median) and as "low users" if not. Also analyzed was the respective impact of the IDA function and teleconsultations on the final HbA1c levels. Among the high users, the proportion of informed meals remained stable from baseline to the end of the study 6months later (from 78.1±21.5% to 73.8±25.1%; P=0.107), but decreased in the low users (from 36.6±29.4% to 26.7±28.4%; P=0.005). As expected, HbA1c improved in high users from 8.7% [range: 8.3-9.2%] to 8.2% [range: 7.8-8.7%]in patients with (n=26) vs without (n=30) the benefit of telemonitoring/teleconsultation (-0.49±0.60% vs -0.52±0.73%, respectively; P=0.879). However, although HbA1c also improved in low users from 9.0% [8.5-10.1] to 8.5% [7.9-9.6], those receiving support via teleconsultation tended to show greater improvement than the others (-0.93±0.97 vs -0.46±1.05, respectively; P=0.084).
input: Question: Telemedicine and type 1 diabetes: is technology per se sufficient to improve glycaemic control?
output: The Diabeo system improved glycaemic control in both high and low users who avidly used the IDA function, while the greatest improvement was seen in the low users who had the motivational support of teleconsultations.
llm_output: The study suggests that while technology, such as the insulin dose advisor (IDA) and telemonitoring/teleconsultation, can support glycaemic control in patients with type 1 diabetes, it is not sufficient on its own. The improvement in HbA1c levels, a key marker of glycaemic control, was more pronounced in high users of the IDA, regardless of whether they had access to teleconsultation. However, the presence of teleconsultation did provide an additional benefit, particularly in low users of the IDA, where the improvement in HbA1c was greater in those receiving teleconsultation support. This indicates that while technology can be a valuable tool, its effectiveness is enhanced when combined with human support and guidance, especially for patients who may not be as actively engaged with the technology. Therefore, the conclusion is that technology alone is not sufficient to improve glycaemic control; it needs to be complemented with clinical support and patient engagement strategies.

instruction: Answer the question based on the following context: Controlled ovarian stimulation (COS) with intrauterine insemination (IUI) is a common treatment in couples with unexplained non-conception. Induction of multifollicular growth is considered to improve pregnancy outcome, but it contains an increased risk of multiple pregnancies and ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome. In this study the impact of the number of follicles (>14 mm) on the ongoing pregnancy rate (PR) and multiple PR was evaluated in the first four treatment cycles. A retrospective cohort study was performed in all couples with unexplained non-conception undergoing COS-IUI in the Academic Hospital of Maastricht. The main outcome measure was ongoing PR. Secondary outcomes were ongoing multiple PR, number of follicles of>or=14 mm, and order of treatment cycle. Three hundred couples were included. No significant difference was found in ongoing PR between women with one, two, three or four follicles respectively (P=0.54), but in women with two or more follicles 12/73 pregnancies were multiples. Ongoing PR was highest in the first treatment cycle and declined significantly with increasing cycle order (P=0.006), while multiple PR did not change.
input: Question: Is controlled ovarian stimulation in intrauterine insemination an acceptable therapy in couples with unexplained non-conception in the perspective of multiple pregnancies?
output: In COS-IUI for unexplained non-conception, induction of more than one follicle did not improve the ongoing PR, but increased the risk of multiple pregnancies. Multiple PR remained high in the first four cycles with multifollicular stimulation. Therefore, in order to reduce the number of multiple pregnancies, in all IUI cycles for unexplained non-conception monofollicular growth should be aimed at.
llm_output: Controlled ovarian stimulation (COS) with intrauterine insemination (IUI) is indeed an accepted and commonly used therapy for couples with unexplained non-conception. The primary goal of this treatment is to increase the chances of pregnancy by stimulating the ovaries to produce multiple follicles, which can then be inseminated with the partner's sperm. However, it is important to consider the potential risks and outcomes associated with this approach, particularly in the context of multiple pregnancies. While the study mentioned indicates that there is no significant difference in ongoing pregnancy rates between women with different numbers of follicles, it does highlight that the risk of multiple pregnancies increases with the number of follicles. Therefore, while COS-IUI is an effective and accepted treatment, it should be used judiciously, taking into account the potential for multiple pregnancies and other complications such as ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome.

instruction: Answer the question based on the following context: To evaluate the usefulness of half-dose contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance (MR) angiography for depicting the abdominal aorta and its major branches. A total of 72 consecutive patients were randomly assigned to one of four groups that underwent MR angiography after receiving different concentrations (original or diluted to 50%) and total amounts (single or half-dose) of gadolinium chelate injected at different rates (1 or 0.5 mL/second). The signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) of the abdominal aorta and of the common and external iliac arteries were calculated, and two blinded readers rated the respective image qualities. The SNR and CNR of the abdominal aorta and the common iliac artery in the 0.5 mL/second groups were statistically significantly lower than those in the 1 mL/second groups. The differences in overall image quality across the four groups were not statistically significant.
input: Question: Is half-dose contrast-enhanced three-dimensional MR angiography sufficient for the abdominal aorta and pelvis?
output: Half-dose MR angiography using diluted contrast medium injected at a rate of 1 mL/second depicted the abdominal aorta and its branches as clearly as using a full single dose.
llm_output: Based on the study, half-dose contrast-enhanced three-dimensional MR angiography can be considered sufficient for the abdominal aorta and pelvis. The research indicates that while the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) in the abdominal aorta and common iliac artery were lower in the half-dose groups, the differences in overall image quality across the four groups (including half-dose and original-dose) were not statistically significant. This suggests that half-dose contrast-enhanced MR angiography, particularly when using a 0.5 mL/second injection rate, may provide adequate image quality for clinical use, although it might not be as optimal as full-dose protocols. The conclusion is supported by the fact that the differences in image quality were not statistically significant, implying that half-dose protocols can be a viable option for reducing contrast agent usage and potentially lowering costs or minimizing side effects.

instruction: Answer the question based on the following context: Digital tomosynthesis (DT) is a new X-ray-based imaging technique that allows image enhancement with minimal increase in radiation exposure. The purpose of this study was to compare DT with noncontrast computed tomography (NCCT) and to evaluate its potential role for the follow-up of patients with nephrolithiasis in a nonemergent setting. A retrospective review of patients with nephrolithiasis at our institution that underwent NCCT and DT from July 2012 to September 2013 was performed. Renal units (RUs) that did not undergo treatment or stone passage were randomly assigned to two blinded readers, who recorded stone count, size area (mm(2)), maximum stone length (mm), and location, for both DT and NCCT. Mean differences per RU were compared. Potential variables affecting stone detection rate, including stone size and body mass index (BMI), were evaluated. Interobserver agreement was determined using the intraclass correlation coefficient to measure the consistency of measurements made by the readers. DT and NCCT demonstrated similar stone detection rates in terms of stone counts and stone area mm(2). Of the 79 RUs assessed, 41 RUs showed exact stone counts on DT and NCCT. The mean difference in stone area was 16.5 mm(2) (-4.6 to 38.5), p = 0.121. The mean size of the largest stone on NCCT and DT was 9.27 and 8.87 mm, respectively. Stone size and BMI did not cause a significant difference in stone detection rates. Interobserver agreement showed a strong correlation between readers and adequate reproducibility.
